records.qualification: Text states that under current adoption scenarios global data-centre demand could almost triple between 2025 and 2030, from about 82 GW to about 220 GW. The sentence carries endnote 1, citing McKinsey's article of 17 December 2025, which is not retained; that is the cited article's publication date and the underlying forecast vintage is unverified. The later text repeats the same rounded global demand value as the August 2025 registration (O09); identical series boundaries and scenario are not established, so no supersession is recorded. Capacity demand, not installed capacity or annual consumption. Ratio for almost triple: about 220 GW in 2030 is the numerator and about 82 GW in 2025 the denominator; N=1 publisher projection linking two endpoint estimates.
records.method_description: Not described beyond the cited December 2025 article; published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

records.scenario: unstated; the page calls the trajectory relatively certain in all scenarios through 2030
records.locator: Section 'How might power demand play out in the next decade?', sentence citing Exhibit 1
records.qualification: Text states that McKinsey's model suggests data-centre power demand could grow about 27 per cent a year through 2030, reaching 121 GW of data-centre IT demand. IT demand, not total facility power. The page assesses US data-centre power demand and calls the trajectory relatively certain in all scenarios through 2030. Endnote 5 separately describes incremental IT demand by 2030 as 121 to 137 GW; how that range relates to the 121 GW text point is unresolved, and Exhibit 1 was not transcribed. Rate: about 27 per cent a year is the stated increase per 100 of the prior year's IT demand; N=1 publisher projection; the retained prose states neither the starting year nor the annual values, which are unverified.
records.method_description: Data-centre evolution scenarios and a state-by-state grid-capacity analysis, as described on the page; published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

records.locator: Section on rising power demand, global capacity sentence following the sentence carrying endnote 10
records.qualification: Text states that global data-centre capacity is expected to grow about 17 per cent a year, reaching about 389 GW by 2035, a 4.6-fold increase. That sentence carries no endnote; endnote 10, citing McKinsey Data Center Solution, is attached to the preceding sentence on data-centre power demand. Worded as capacity; the retained prose does not say whether installed or demanded and does not state the starting year of the 4.6-fold increase. Exhibit 3 was not transcribed. Rate and multiple: about 17 per cent a year is the stated increase per 100 of the prior year's capacity; the 4.6-fold increase takes capacity in 2035, about 389 GW, as numerator and capacity in the unstated starting year as denominator, which is unverified and is not derived here from the rounded multiple; N=1 publisher projection.
records.method_description: The capacity sentence has no endnote; endnote 10 cites McKinsey Data Center Solution for the preceding power-demand sentence; published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

records.qualification: Text states that, according to Deloitte estimates, data-centre electricity demand could rise five-fold by 2035, reaching 176 GW. The sentence does not name a geography; US is inferred from the article's US context and from Deloitte's February 2026 article (S21), which restates 176 GW for data centres nationally in a US article. Power in GW, not annual energy. The retained prose does not state the base year of the five-fold increase; Figure 1 was not transcribed. Endnote 1 names the analysis inputs, including data from DC Byte and Wells Fargo and LBNL's 2024 data-centre energy report. This establishes an input link to an earlier LBNL report; exact shared inputs with the registered later LBNL update are not established. Agreement therefore cannot automatically be treated as independent confirmation. The calculation method is not described. Multiple: five-fold takes demand in 2035, 176 GW, as numerator and demand in the unstated base year as denominator, which is unverified and is not derived here from the rounded multiple; N=1 publisher estimate.
records.method_description: Deloitte Research Center analysis of named external data and studies (endnote 1); method not described; published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

scope_limits: Convenience sample of existing named institutions; not a census or forecast-accuracy test.
Source matching confirms what publishers state, not that the forecasts are true.
No underlying provider model has been reconstructed in this revision.
Unresolved sources are retained separately and excluded from calculated envelopes.
Recorded-value spans list superseded same-publisher vintages separately and retain scope, scenario and shape mismatches; no pooled consensus, uplift or model ranking is calculated.
No metres, site inspections or realised national US data-centre outcome series were collected.
A document available publicly does not prove that its complete input data and executable model are public.

Disclosed input links among registered providers: the IEA model relies on a bottom-up approach developed by LBNL (S02, Annex A methodology); Goldman Sachs uses a 451 Research data set (S09); Deloitte's November 2024 estimate cites Goldman Sachs and EPRI among its sources (S13, endnote 1), which predates their later registered observations; Deloitte's April 2025 estimate names LBNL's 2024 data-centre energy report among its inputs (S20, endnote 1), an earlier report than the registered LBNL 2025 update (S03). Agreement among linked providers cannot automatically be counted as independent confirmation; the exact shared inputs and vintages are not established.

Support review receipts bind each observation and the complete source catalogue by digest. A currency sweep on 8 October 2026 searched each registered publisher for newer editions; it is a bounded search, not proof that no newer forecast exists.

field_definitions.shape: point: a single stated value; scenario_range: stated scenario bounds with an optional reference point; upper_bound: only an upper value is stated, so low and point are null. lower_bound: only a lower value is stated, so high and point are null; whether the bound is inclusive is stated in the qualification.
field_definitions.value_basis: Whether the registered figure is a table value, a text value or a chart label.
field_definitions.coverage: total_facility_IT_plus_overhead: total consumption including facility overhead, as distinct from IT-only; data_centres_unspecified: the facility boundary is not fully stated, and stated workload or developer dimensions are not a complete boundary. it_load: IT demand only, excluding facility overhead. new_data_centres_unspecified: the figure covers new data centres only, and its facility boundary is not fully stated.
field_definitions.superseded_by: A later vintage of the same publisher series and quantity, not necessarily the immediately following one.
field_definitions.crypto_scope: excluded_inferred: the exclusion is stated for a related calculation and applied to this series by inference.
field_definitions.metric: data_centre_capacity_demand: power demand stated in GW; data_centre_capacity: capacity stated in GW without saying whether installed or demanded; installed_capacity: capacity stated as expected online; annual_electricity: energy in TWh.
field_definitions.unit: TWh: annual energy; GW: power or capacity; percent_growth: growth relative to base_year. A value the source states in another unit of the same quantity, such as MW, is recorded after an exact conversion, which the qualification states.
